Select

Select components allow users to choose one option from a list. ZAKUIKit provides styled native selects with multiple variants.

Basic Select

A standard native select element with ZAKUIKit styling.

HTML 
<select class="zak-select">
  <option value="">Select an option</option>
  <option value="1">Option 1</option>
  <option value="2">Option 2</option>
  <option value="3">Option 3</option>
</select>

Option Groups

Group related options with <optgroup>.

HTML 
<select class="zak-select">
  <option value="">Choose a framework</option>
  <optgroup label="JavaScript">
    <option value="react">React</option>
    <option value="vue">Vue.js</option>
    <option value="angular">Angular</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="CSS">
    <option value="tailwind">Tailwind CSS</option>
    <option value="bootstrap">Bootstrap</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

Disabled Options

Disable specific options or the entire select.

HTML 
<select class="zak-select">
  <option value="">Select a plan</option>
  <option value="free">Free</option>
  <option value="pro">Pro</option>
  <option value="enterprise" disabled>Enterprise (Coming Soon)</option>
</select>

<select class="zak-select" disabled>
  <option>Cannot change this</option>
</select>

Sizes

Select inputs support small, default, and large sizes.

HTML 
<select class="zak-select zak-select-sm">...</select>
<select class="zak-select">...</select>
<select class="zak-select zak-select-lg">...</select>

Validation States

Show success or error states on selects.

Country selected successfully.
Please select a valid country.
HTML 
<select class="zak-select zak-form-control-success">...</select>
<select class="zak-select zak-form-control-danger">...</select>

CSS Classes Reference

Class Description
.zak-selectBase select styling
.zak-select-smSmall size
.zak-select-lgLarge size
.zak-form-control-successSuccess state
.zak-form-control-dangerError state

Accessibility

  • Every select must have a visible <label> associated via for/id.
  • The first option should act as a placeholder with an empty value.
  • Use <optgroup> labels to help screen readers understand groupings.
  • Disabled options should be clearly indicated with the disabled attribute.
  • Ensure keyboard navigation works — users should be able to tab to and arrow through options.
